output: html_document
---
1. Load the spotify dataset (available in github repository).
```{r}
spotifyDat.Fall26 <- read.csv("~/Downloads/spotifyDat Fall26.csv")
```

2. Create a bar graph of the artist column (Hint: use theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90)) to rotate the x axis).
```{r}
ggplot(spotifyDat.Fall26,aes(x=artist))+geom_bar()+theme(axis.text.x=element_text(angle= 90))
```

3. Add genre as a third variable in your graph.
```{r}
ggplot(spotifyDat.Fall26, aes(x = artist, fill = genre)) +geom_bar() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90))
```

4. Use color brewer to add color to your graph in 3. 
```{r}
ggplot(spotifyDat.Fall26, aes(x = artist, fill = genre)) +geom_bar() +scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set5") +theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90))
```

5. Place the legend for the graph you made in 3 on the bottom of the graph. 
```{r}
ggplot(spotifyDat.Fall26, aes(x = artist, fill = genre)) +geom_bar() +theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90),legend.position = "bottom")
```

As you probably recognized, the graph you made is really hard to read.

6. Separate the genre column into multiple columns (e.g. so each genre listed is in a unique column)
```{r}
spotifySeparate <- spotifyDat.Fall26 |>separate(genre, into = c("genre1", "genre2", "genre3", "genre4"), sep = ", ")
```

7. Use these genre columns to create a dataset in long format. 
```{r}
spotifyLong <- spotifySeparate |> pivot_longer(cols = genre1:genre4,names_to = "genre_number",values_to = "genre")
```

8.use facet wrap to make graphs of artist by genre 
```{r}
ggplot(spotifyLong, aes(x = artist)) +geom_bar() +facet_wrap(~genre) +theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90))
```

9. Create a graph that includes the variables tempo and dancability. 
```{r}
ggplot(spotifyDat.Fall26, aes(x = tempo, y = danceability)) +geom_point()
```

10. Add popularity as a third variable. 
```{r}
ggplot(spotifyDat.Fall26,aes(x = tempo, y = danceability, color = popularity)) +geom_point()
```

11. Use viridis as a color in your graph from #10
```{r}
ggplot(spotifyDat.Fall26, aes(x = tempo, y = danceability, color = popularity)) +geom_point() +scale_color_viridis()

```
